# Start here

This guide explains the package as it is now, top to bottom. It is the one to read first; the other
documents go deep on one topic each:

| document | topic |
|---|---|
| **00 (this one)** | layout, data flow, AOT compilation, concurrency and locking, imports |
| 01 | concurrency in ROS 2 / Python from first principles (executors, GIL, processes, GC) |
| 02 | the multithreaded node: options, benchmarks, flight recorder |
| 03 | AOT compilation, early-exit rollouts, wind estimation, what caused the crashes |
| 04 | GP feedforward, ground floor, LAND backup, the spatial certificate |
| 06 | five model fixes (feedback sign, Jacobian domain, row lookup, body-frame velocities, 100 Hz state) and the TV-GPR / GPR × embedding-system comparison |
| 05 (`cpp-version`) | the C++ fast loop |

Code references are `path:line` relative to `packages/px4_rta_mm_gpr/` unless stated otherwise.

# The repository

```text
PX4_RTA_MM_GPR/
  README.md
  docs/                 .qmd sources, PDFs in _output/, figure scripts
  tools/run_sitl.sh     PX4 SITL with this project's parameters
  packages/             colcon --base-paths PX4_RTA_MM_GPR/packages
    flight_recorder/    submodule: HDF5 logging (Python + C++ header)
    px4_rta_mm_gpr/     the ROS 2 package (ament_python)
      package.xml, setup.py, setup.cfg, resource/
      launch/           sim_rta_launch.py, only_full_state_relay_launch.py
      scripts/
        px4_rta_mm_gpr.py   entry point: options, executor, shutdown
        rta_mm_gpr_node.py  OffboardControl: callbacks, shared state
        data_analysis/      notebooks 01-04, figures/, log_files/
      px4_rta_mm_gpr/   the library (no ROS, except px4_functions)
        jax_mm_rta/     planar model, TVGPR/GPR, rollout, certificate
        jax_nr/         Newton-Raphson tracker (pitch, yaw rates)
        control_kernels.py  AOT: control_step, wind_model, linearize
        concurrency/    RolloutPlan, RolloutEngine, backends, LoopStats
        flight_log/     the node's recorder, the log reader
        px4_functions/  arm, land, heartbeat, setpoints
        utilities/      jax_setup, vehicle constants, yaw unwrapping
        sim/            numerical closed-loop simulation
        analysis.py     summaries, plots, tube videos
      test/             pytest: sim + analysis, certificate, lint
```

**Why `packages/`.** colcon finds a package by its `package.xml`, and it does not look inside another
package's directory. With `flight_recorder` (and, on `cpp-version`, two C++ packages) living in this
repository, each package needs its own directory next to the others; `packages/` holds them.

**How it builds.** `px4_rta_mm_gpr` is an `ament_python` package: colcon runs `setup.py`, which installs
the library (`find_packages` finds `px4_rta_mm_gpr` and `scripts`), `package.xml` and the launch files,
and creates two console scripts:

| command | runs |
|---|---|
| `ros2 run px4_rta_mm_gpr px4_rta_mm_gpr` | `scripts/px4_rta_mm_gpr.py:main` (the node) |
| `ros2 run px4_rta_mm_gpr flight_log` | `px4_rta_mm_gpr/flight_log/reader.py:main` (summary / CSV export of a log) |

`flight_recorder` is an `ament_cmake` package (it installs a Python module *and* a C++ header), so
`colcon build` builds both from one command. With `--symlink-install` the installed Python files are
symlinks to the sources: edits take effect without rebuilding.

**Outside dependencies.** `px4_msgs` (PX4's ROS 2 messages, in `~/ws_sensor_combined`),
and pip packages: `jax`, `immrax`, `control`, `scipy`, `h5py`, `pandas`,
`matplotlib`, `imageio-ffmpeg`.

# What happens when you run it

`ros2 launch px4_rta_mm_gpr sim_rta_launch.py` runs
`px4_rta_mm_gpr --sim --log-file log.log`. Then:

1. **`main()`** (`scripts/px4_rta_mm_gpr.py`) parses the options into a frozen `RuntimeOptions`
   dataclass and computes the log path, `<workspace>/src/data_analysis/log_files/px4_rta_mm_gpr/`.
2. **`rclpy.init()`**, then **`OffboardControl(sim, options)`** (`scripts/rta_mm_gpr_node.py:190`). The
   constructor does all the slow work *before* anything flies:
   a. vehicle constants (`utilities/sim_utilities.py` or `hardware_utilities.py`), wind EKF,
      callback groups, publishers and subscriptions;
   b. `init_jit_compile_nr_rta()`: tunables, GP buffers, `RolloutConfig`, then **compilation**:
      the rollout worker process is spawned first (it compiles the rollout in parallel), then the
      control kernels are compiled ahead of time, the first LQR gains computed, and the node waits for
      the worker's "ready" (about 4.4 s in total with a warm disk cache);
   c. the `FlightRecorder` is created with every option as metadata;
   d. `gc.collect(); gc.freeze()` and the generation-2 threshold is raised (see Concurrency);
   e. the **timers are created last**, so no callback runs before the constructor finishes.
3. The **executor** is built (`--executor multi|single|events`) and `executor.spin()` runs the callbacks.
   With autosave on, the recorder flushes to disk every 5 s from its own thread.
4. The **mission**, on the node's clock `t = now() - T0`:

| time | who flies | what the node does |
|---|---|---|
| $t < 15$ s | PX4 position controller | position setpoint (0, 4, −12.5) m in SITL; heartbeat; after 10 heartbeats: offboard + arm; warm-up rollouts |
| $15 \le t < 35$ s | **this node** | 100 Hz body-rate + thrust commands from the certified plan; wind EKF and GP learning; replanning |
| $t \ge 35$ s | PX4 | position setpoint above the origin, then land and disarm |

   At any time in the RTA window, if no certified plan exists for more than 20 ms
   (`--backup-grace`), the node commands PX4 **LAND** and stops sending commands.
5. **Shutdown** (Ctrl-C, or the end of `launch`): `close()` stops the worker process and prints the
   timing summary; `save_flight_log()` writes the HDF5 file (and the legacy CSV next to it).

## One control tick (100 Hz, control group)

`control_algorithm_callback` → `control_administrator` (`scripts/rta_mm_gpr_node.py:989`):

1. read `s = self.state` and `plan = self.plan` **once** (they may be replaced at any moment);
2. if `t > plan.collection_time` the plan is no longer certified: count it, and after 20 ms
   continuously uncertified, `engage_backup()` → PX4 LAND;
3. `traj_idx = plan.index_at(t)`: the plan row for *now*, computed from time, not from a tick counter;
4. **one** compiled call, `kernels.control_step(...)`: the NR tracker (pitch and yaw rates) and the RTA
   feedback `u = clip(u_ff[i] - K (x - x_ref[i]))` (thrust and roll rate), clipped;
5. thrust → throttle (`get_throttle_command_from_force`), publish the body-rate setpoint;
6. one row into the recorder's `ticks` buffer.

## One plan (rollout group, and the worker process)

`rollout_callback` (`:765`) runs every 10 ms but only starts a rollout when it is due:

1. `poll()` the backend; a finished result is **installed** (`install_plan`, `:843`): it becomes an
   immutable `RolloutPlan`, is published with one assignment `self.plan = plan`, and stored in the log;
2. a rollout is due when `t >= collection_time - lead`, where `collection_time` is when the current
   plan stops being certified and `lead` is about twice the recent worst rollout latency
   (**pre-emptive replanning**: the next plan is installed before the current one expires);
3. the request is a **snapshot**: `RolloutRequest(t, state, K_feedback, K_reference, obs_wy, obs_wz,
   goal)`, all values copied or immutable at that moment;
4. the engine runs the compiled rollout: the reference trajectory under the reference LQR, and the
   **mixed-monotone embedding** that bounds every state the vehicle can reach, given the GP's wind
   bounds (mean ± 3σ plus a Lipschitz buffer). It stops at the **first row that fails the certificate**
   plus a 1 s margin (early exit);
5. the certificate is **spatial**: a row fails when the tube's position bounds ($p_y$ or $p_z$) are more
   than 0.25 m + δ from the reference position, or the tube reaches the 0.3 m floor. δ is the
   position-estimate uncertainty carried by the request (0 in sim, 3σ of EKF2 on hardware); it also widens
   the initial box (doc 04).

## Wind and gains (state and estimation groups)

* **Wind EKF** at the odometry rate (100 Hz), in the state thread, only while this node's commands fly:
  measured acceleration minus the model's (the compiled `wind_model`) is the wind force estimate
  (`self.wy`, `self.wz`).
* **GP data**, 10 Hz, estimation thread: one row per buffer (time, input, wind): the y-wind is learned as a
  function of altitude, the z-wind as a function of lateral position. Each buffer is a 9-row ring,
  updated **copy-on-write** (see Locks).
* **LQR**, estimation thread: re-linearise the planar model (compiled `linearize`) and solve two LQRs
  (`control.lqr`) every 1.8 s, or when the yaw error exceeds 5°. The pair of gains is published as one
  tuple.

# Ahead-of-time JAX compilation

## What JAX does with a function

JAX turns a Python function into an XLA program in two steps:

1. **Tracing.** JAX calls the function with *abstract* arguments (only shapes and dtypes) and records
   every `jnp` operation into a graph (a *jaxpr*). Python control flow runs once, at trace time; loops
   that must stay loops use `lax.scan`, `lax.while_loop` or `lax.fori_loop`.
2. **Compilation.** XLA optimises the graph (fusing operations, choosing memory layouts) and emits machine
   code for the CPU. Running it later costs microseconds to milliseconds; compiling costs 0.1–10 s.

`jax.jit(f)` does both lazily, at the first call, and **caches one executable per call signature**: the
shapes and dtypes of the arguments, but also details that are easy to miss: a Python `float` is a
*weakly typed* scalar while a float64 array is not; an array already on the device is *committed*.
Any difference means a new trace and a new compile.

## Why the node compiles ahead of time

The original node "warmed up" by calling each jitted function once in `__init__`. In flight, one argument
(`last_input`) became the controller's own output array: a different signature, so XLA compiled again
**in the air** (322 ms: 32 missed control ticks), plus more compiles for slicing and concatenation.

AOT compilation removes the possibility:

```python
f64 = lambda *shape: jax.ShapeDtypeStruct(shape, jnp.float64)
compiled = jax.jit(control_step).lower(f64(9), f64(5), f64(4), ...).compile()
```

* `lower(...)` traces for exactly these shapes and dtypes, **without calling** the function;
* `.compile()` returns a `jax.stages.Compiled`: one executable, one signature. **It never recompiles.**
  Called with anything else it raises `TypeError` immediately, which is what you want to find out on the
  bench, not in flight;
* every in-flight argument goes through `as_f64(x, shape)` (`control_kernels.py:36`):
  `np.ascontiguousarray(x, dtype=np.float64).reshape(shape)`. One canonical type, always.

## What is compiled

| executable | built in | inputs → outputs | used by |
|-----|------------|--------------|------|
| `control_step` | `control_kernels.py:54` | states, last input, NR reference, plan row, gains → 4 commands | control thread, 100 Hz |
| `wind_model` | `control_kernels.py:61` | NR state, input → model accelerations | state thread, 100 Hz |
| `linearize` | `control_kernels.py:65` | planar state, input → $A, B$ (`jax.jacfwd`) | estimation thread |
| rollout | `rollout_backends.py:131` | $t_0$, state, $x_\text{pert}$, gains, 2 GP buffers, goal, threshold (y, z) → tube, reference, feedforward, violation row, rows used | rollout thread or worker process |

`control_step` **fuses** what used to be about six separate dispatches per tick (NR tracker, slicing,
`u_applied`, concatenation, clipping) into one executable: one call from Python per tick.

**Static vs traced arguments.** In the rollout, the things that never change during a flight (horizon,
time step, the planar system, its mixed Jacobian, input limits, threshold, floor) are bound with
`functools.partial` *before* lowering: they are constants of the compiled program. Only the eight
arrays in the table are traced inputs.

**Fixed shapes with early exit.** XLA programs have fixed shapes. The early-exit rollout
(`jax_mm_rta/mm_rta.py:307`) uses `lax.while_loop` over preallocated full-horizon arrays filled with NaN
and returns `n_valid`, the number of rows it actually computed; the engine trims the result in NumPy.
The loop stops at the first failing row plus the margin (3–7 ms instead of 60–190 ms for the full 30 s),
and the rows it computes are identical to the full rollout's (it only depends on earlier rows).

## Configuration and the disk cache

`utilities/jax_setup.py` is imported **before anything is compiled** (every module that compiles imports
it first):

* `jax_enable_x64 = True`: float64 everywhere (the default is float32);
* `jax_compilation_cache_dir = ~/.cache/px4_rta_mm_gpr/jax`: compiled executables are written to disk and
  reused by later runs *and by the worker process*. Start-up compilation went from about 20 s to about
  4–6 s. `PX4_RTA_JAX_CACHE=''` disables it. Changing the code of a compiled function changes its key, so
  the cache never serves a stale executable.

## Practical rules

* A new argument shape (e.g. more GP rows, a longer horizon) needs a change where the shapes are declared
  (`_shapes` in `RolloutEngine`, the `lower(...)` calls in `ControlKernels`). It then fails loudly at
  start-up, never silently in flight.
* Keep Python control flow on *static* values; anything that depends on array values must be `jnp.where`,
  `lax.cond` or a `lax` loop.
* JAX arrays are immutable: `a.at[i].set(v)` returns a *new* array. (The original GP buffers used
  `.at[].set()` and discarded the result, so the GP never learned; they are NumPy arrays now.)

# Concurrency

## Threads, the GIL and XLA

A Python process runs one interpreter with one **global interpreter lock** (GIL): only one thread executes
Python bytecode at a time. Threads still help here because the heavy work is not Python: a compiled XLA
executable **releases the GIL** while it runs, and so do NumPy's large operations and DDS I/O. While the
rollout's executable runs on XLA's thread pool, the control thread holds the GIL for its ~0.2 ms tick
and continues on schedule. Doc 01 has the full story with timelines.

## Executors

An rclpy **executor** waits for ready timers and messages and runs their callbacks. `--executor`:

| option | what it is | callbacks run |
|-----|-----------|---------|
| `multi` (default) | `MultiThreadedExecutor`, 5 threads | in parallel across callback groups |
| `single` | `SingleThreadedExecutor` (the original `rclpy.spin`) | one at a time |
| `events` | `EventsExecutor` (`rclpy.experimental`) | one at a time; the wait/dispatch loop is C++ (much less overhead) |

## Callback groups

A **mutually exclusive callback group** never runs two of its callbacks at the same time; different
groups may run in parallel on a multithreaded executor. Five groups, so five threads are enough:

| group | callbacks (period) | writes |
|-------|--------|---------|
| `px4_io_group` | heartbeat (0.1 s), `vehicle_status`, RC channels | offboard / armed / RC flags; PX4 mode and arm commands |
| `state_group` | PX4 `vehicle_odometry` (100 Hz) + wind EKF; `vehicle_local_position` (50 Hz, acceleration) | `self.state`, `self.wy`, `self.wz`, `self.position_sigma`, recorder `wind` |
| `control_group` | control law (0.01 s) | `self.last_input`, recorder `ticks`, setpoints to PX4 |
| `rollout_group` | rollout check (0.01 s) | `self.plan`, `self.collection_time`, recorder plans |
| `estimation_group` | GP buffers (0.1 s), LQR check (0.05 s) | GP buffers, `self.gains`, recorder `gains` |

The rule that makes this work: **each piece of shared state has exactly one writer thread**. Readers in
other threads only ever take a snapshot.

## Where the rollout runs (`--rollout-backend`)

`concurrency/rollout_backends.py` hides *where* the rollout runs behind `submit(request)` / `poll()`:

* **`thread`**: `submit` computes synchronously in the rollout group's executor thread. With `multi`, that
  thread is separate from control, and XLA releases the GIL, so control keeps its schedule.
* **`process`** (recommended, with `--executor events`): a separate OS process with its own interpreter,
  GIL and JAX runtime. `submit` sends the pickled `RolloutRequest` through a `multiprocessing.Pipe` and
  returns at once; `poll()` checks the pipe without blocking. Even a single-threaded executor then never
  waits for a rollout. Details:
  * start method **`spawn`**, not `fork`: forking a process that already runs JAX/XLA and DDS threads can
    deadlock the child; `spawn` starts a fresh interpreter that imports only what it needs;
  * the worker is started **first** in `__init__`, so its compilation overlaps with the node's;
  * `RolloutConfig` (static) is sent once at start; each request/result is a small frozen dataclass of
    NumPy arrays (cheap to pickle); the result arrays are trimmed to `n_valid` rows;
  * `--rollout-cpus 2,3` pins the worker to CPUs (`os.sched_setaffinity`), away from the control thread;
  * a worker exception is sent back as `('error', traceback)` and raised in the node, never lost.

## Garbage collection

CPython frees most objects by reference counting; a separate **cycle collector** runs in generations. A
full (generation 2) collection walks every tracked object **while holding the GIL**: measured ~300 ms,
i.e. 30 missed ticks, and the JAX/immrax start-up creates hundreds of thousands of long-lived objects.

* `gc.freeze()` after start-up moves all of them to a permanent generation that is never scanned again
  (about 296 000 objects);
* `--gc-no-full` raises the generation-2 threshold so no full collection runs in flight (young
  collections still run, ~1 ms); one full collection runs at shutdown;
* a `gc.callbacks` hook measures every in-flight pause and puts it in the log.

## Timing statistics

`LoopStats` (`concurrency/loop_stats.py`) wraps each periodic callback in a context manager that records
the actual period and execution time into preallocated arrays, under its own small lock. The summary at
shutdown ("control: rate 100.0 Hz, period p99 10.3 ms, misses 0") and the log's `records/timing/` come
from it.

# Shared state and locks

## The pattern: build, then publish with one assignment

Most of the node's sharing uses **no lock** at all. A writer builds a complete, immutable object and
publishes it by assigning one attribute; a reader reads the attribute **once** and works with that object:

```python
# rollout thread (writer)             # control thread (reader)
plan = RolloutPlan(...)  # complete    plan = self.plan        # ONE read
self.plan = plan         # publish     row = plan.index_at(t)  # consistent
```

In CPython, assigning an attribute (a reference) is atomic with respect to other threads: a reader sees the
old object or the new one, never a mixture. The objects are never modified after publication (frozen
dataclasses, tuples; by convention the NumPy arrays inside them are not written either), so the reader
needs no lock for as long as it uses them. The same idea in C++ is `std::atomic<std::shared_ptr<const T>>`
(the fast loop on `cpp-version`).

What goes wrong without it: the original node kept `self.x`, `self.y`, `self.vx`, … as separate
attributes updated one by one; another thread could read a new position with an old velocity. The same for
a plan whose tube and reference were assigned separately.

## Every shared variable

| shared | written by | read by | mechanism |
|-------|-----|------|--------|
| `self.state` (`VehicleState`) | state | control, rollout, estimation | frozen dataclass, one assignment |
| `self.plan` (`RolloutPlan`) | rollout | control, px4_io (status line) | frozen dataclass, one assignment; `plan_lock` around installation |
| `self.gains` (`(K_fb, K_ref)`) | estimation | control, rollout | tuple, one assignment (both gains always from the same linearisation) |
| GP buffers `obs_wy`, `obs_wz` | estimation | rollout (into the request) | copy-on-write: copy, modify the copy, assign |
| `self.wy`, `self.wz` | state | estimation, control (logged) | floats, one assignment each |
| `self.position_sigma` (EKF2 σ, y and z) | state | rollout (into the request's δ) | a new array, one assignment |
| `self.last_input` | control | state (wind model) | a new array each tick, one assignment |
| offboard / armed / RC flags | px4_io | control, heartbeat | bools |
| warm-up request | estimation | rollout | `threading.Event` |
| recorder streams | one thread each (ticks: control, wind: state, gains: estimation) | autosave thread | `ColumnBuffer`: row written, *then* the count published |
| recorder records / events | rollout (plans), control (events) | autosave thread | `Recorder._lock` |
| `LoopStats` samples | the measured callback | shutdown summary | `LoopStats._lock` |

## The locks there are, and why

* **`plan_lock`** (`threading.Lock`, `rta_mm_gpr_node.py:324`): held while a plan is installed, so the
  plan number, `collection_time` and the new plan are updated together. The control thread never takes
  it; it reads `self.plan` once (the plan itself carries its own `collection_time`).
* **`Recorder._lock`** (flight_recorder): guards the lists of records and events and the stream registry.
  Appending a record and the autosave thread's snapshot of "what is new since the last flush" are short
  critical sections.
* **`Recorder._flush_lock`**: one flush at a time (the autosave thread and the final `save()` could
  otherwise both write the file).
* **`Recorder._stop`** (`threading.Event`): tells the autosave thread to stop; `save()` joins it before the
  final flush.
* **`LoopStats._lock`**: the measured thread appends while the shutdown code may read.
* **No lock in `ColumnBuffer.append`**: each stream has one writer; the row is written first and the row
  count incremented after it, so a concurrent reader (the autosave flush) sees only complete rows. When the
  buffer grows, it copies into a new array and swaps the reference; a reader holding the old array still
  has valid rows.

**A known, harmless race.** `self.wy, self.wz = wy, wz` is two assignments, so a reader could pair a new
`wy` with the previous `wz` (25 ms older). Both are slowly varying estimates that only feed the GP buffers
and the log; if they ever had to be consistent, they would become one tuple, like the gains.

# The control law, the model and the GP (in brief)

* **Planar model** (`jax_mm_rta/mm_rta.py:75`): state $(p_y, p_z, h, v, \theta)$ with body-frame
  velocities $h, v$; inputs thrust $u_1$ and roll rate $u_2$; wind forces $w_y, w_z$.
* **TVGPR** (`jax_mm_rta/TVGPR.py`): time-varying GP regression, squared-exponential kernel in space times a
  forgetting factor $(1-\epsilon)^{|t-t'|/2}$ in time, 9 observations per GP. `GPR.py` is the
  time-invariant variant, kept as part of the package API.
* **Rollout step** (`_make_step`): the reference moves under the reference LQR (plus the GP mean
  feedforward on thrust); the tube moves under the **embedding system** built from immrax's mixed
  Jacobians (`irx.mjacM`) of the dynamics and of the GP mean, with the wind interval from the GP.
* **NR tracker** (`jax_nr/`): predicts the output 0.8 s ahead (forward Euler in a `lax.fori_loop`), inverts
  the Jacobian of that prediction with respect to the input, and adds an integral control-barrier term that
  keeps the rates within ±0.8 rad/s. It flies pitch and yaw; the RTA feedback flies thrust and roll.

# Logging, analysis and simulation reuse the same parts

* **Flight log** (`flight_log/recorder.py` on `flight_recorder`): streams `ticks`, `wind`, `gains`; every plan
  stored once with the inputs that produced it (`records/plans/<seq>`); timing arrays; events; all options
  as metadata. Autosaved every 5 s.
* **Numerical simulation** (`sim/planar.py`): the same `RolloutEngine`, `ControlKernels`, `u_applied` and
  `FlightRecorder`, around an RK4 integration of the planar model and a known wind field (`sim/wind.py`). It
  writes the same log format, so the analysis works on it unchanged.
* **Analysis** (`analysis.py`): summaries, plots, the `PlanGP` reconstruction of the exact GP a plan used,
  `tube_violation` (why a certificate ended) and `animate` (the tube videos).

# Every import, and what it is for

## Standard library

| import | what it is | used for |
|-------------|------|---------|
| `os` | operating-system interface | paths, `makedirs`, environment (`PX4_RTA_JAX_CACHE`), `sched_setaffinity` (worker CPUs) |
| `sys` | interpreter access | `sys.argv` for the command line |
| `time` | clocks | `time.time()` (node clock, latencies), `perf_counter()` (compute times, compile times) |
| `threading` | threads and synchronisation | `Lock` (`plan_lock`, `LoopStats`), `Event` (warm-up request), recorder autosave thread |
| `multiprocessing` | processes | `get_context('spawn')`, `Process`, `Pipe` for the rollout worker |
| `gc` | the cycle garbage collector | `freeze`, `set_threshold`, `callbacks` (pause measurement), `get_objects` (heap summary) |
| `argparse` | command-line parsing | every `--option` of the node |
| `dataclasses` | `@dataclass` | frozen, immutable snapshots: `RuntimeOptions`, `VehicleState`, `RolloutPlan`, `RolloutConfig/Request/Result`, `SimConfig` |
| `typing` | type hints | `Optional`, `Sequence`, `Dict`, `Callable`, `Tuple` (documentation and editors) |
| `from __future__ import annotations` | lazy annotations | type hints are not evaluated at import time (cheaper, allows forward references) |
| `partial` (`functools`) | bind arguments | fix the rollout's static arguments before lowering; `@partial(jax.jit, static_argnames=...)` |
| `contextmanager` (`contextlib`) | generator-based `with` blocks | `LoopStats.measure()` |
| `inspect`, `traceback` | introspection, stack traces | name the failing function and print the full trace in error handlers; ship worker errors to the node |
| `math` | scalar math | thrust → throttle conversion in the vehicle constants |
| `glob` | file patterns | `setup.py` (launch files), notebooks (log files) |
| `textwrap` | text wrapping | reasons in the videos |
| `Counter` (`collections`) | counting | heap summary (object types the GC scans) |

## ROS 2

| import | what it is | used for |
|-------------|------|---------|
| `rclpy` | the ROS 2 Python client library | `init`, `ok`, `shutdown` |
| `Node` (`rclpy.node`) | base class of a node | `OffboardControl` subclasses it: publishers, subscriptions, timers, logger |
| `MutuallyExclusiveCallbackGroup` (`rclpy.callback_groups`) | callback groups | the five groups above |
| `QoSProfile`, `ReliabilityPolicy`, `HistoryPolicy`, `DurabilityPolicy` (`rclpy.qos`) | quality of service | PX4's topics need best-effort, transient-local, depth 1 |
| `SingleThreadedExecutor`, `MultiThreadedExecutor` (`rclpy.executors`); `EventsExecutor` (`rclpy.experimental`) | executors | `--executor` |
| `px4_msgs.msg` | PX4's uORB messages as ROS 2 types | `OffboardControlMode`, `VehicleCommand`, `TrajectorySetpoint`, `VehicleRatesSetpoint` (out); `VehicleStatus`, `RcChannels`, `VehicleOdometry` (state + EKF2 position variance, 100 Hz), `VehicleLocalPosition` (acceleration, 50 Hz) (in) |
| `launch`, `Node` (`launch_ros.actions`) | ROS 2 launch system | the launch files |
| `setuptools` | Python packaging | `setup.py` (`find_packages`, entry points, data files) |

## Numerics and control

| import | what it is | used for |
|-------------|------|---------|
| `numpy` | arrays | everything outside compiled code: states, buffers, the EKF, logging, canonical `float64` arguments |
| `jax`, `jax.numpy as jnp` | NumPy-like arrays + tracing + XLA compilation + automatic differentiation | the model, GPs, rollout, NR tracker; `jax.jit(...).lower(...).compile()`, `ShapeDtypeStruct`, `jacfwd`, `vmap`, `config` |
| `jax.lax` (`scan`, `while_loop`, `fori_loop`, `cond`) | structured control flow that stays inside the compiled program | the full-horizon rollout, the early-exit rollout, NR's prediction loop, the certificate test |
| `jacfwd`, `jacrev`, `hessian` (`jax`) | automatic differentiation | NR's Jacobian of the prediction; `linearize` for the LQR |
| `immrax as irx` | interval analysis and mixed-monotone reachability on JAX | `irx.interval`, `icentpert` (initial box), `i2ut`/`ut2i` (interval ↔ embedding vector), `mjacM`/`jacM` (mixed Jacobian bounds), `ifemb` (embedding system), `Permutation`, `System` (base class of the planar model) |
| `control` (python-control) | control-systems toolbox | `control.lqr(A, B, Q, R)` for both gain matrices |
| `Rotation` (`scipy.spatial.transform`) | rotations | quaternion → roll, pitch, yaw in the odometry callback |

# Where to change what

| to … | change |
|------|---------|
| add a command-line option | `argparse` in `scripts/px4_rta_mm_gpr.py`, a field in `RuntimeOptions`, use `self.options.<name>` |
| compare wind models / embedding systems | `--gp tv\|static`, `--embedding uw\|u\|none` (node); `SimConfig(gp_epsilon=..., embedding=...)`; notebook 05 |
| change what the certificate tests | `_row_fails` and `collection_id_jax` (`jax_mm_rta/mm_rta.py`), `tube_violation` (`analysis.py`), the test in `test/test_sim_analysis.py` |
| log a new per-tick value | `TICK_COLUMNS` and `tick()` in `flight_log/recorder.py` (same order) |
| add a new periodic job | a timer in a callback group; if it writes shared state, publish it as one immutable object |
| change an input shape of a compiled kernel | the `lower(...)` shapes (`ControlKernels`, `RolloutEngine._shapes`) and the `as_f64` reshapes |
| run without ROS | `px4_rta_mm_gpr.sim.simulate(SimConfig(...), winds=...)` |

# Glossary

AOT
: ahead-of-time compilation: compiling for a declared signature before the first call.

callback group
: a set of callbacks that an executor never runs concurrently (mutually exclusive).

certificate / certified horizon
: the time span over which the reachable tube stays within 0.25 m of the reference position and above the
  floor; the plan may be flown only within it.

copy-on-write
: modify a copy, then replace the shared reference with it.

embedding system
: a system of twice the dimension whose state is a lower and an upper bound; its trajectory bounds every
  trajectory of the original system (mixed monotonicity).

GIL
: CPython's global interpreter lock: one thread runs Python bytecode at a time.

snapshot
: an immutable object read once and used for the rest of a callback.

XLA
: the compiler behind JAX; compiled programs run on its own threads and release the GIL.
